question: In primary congenital glaucoma, elevated IOP results from trabeculodysgenesis — an arrest of embryological angle maturation — causing increased resistance to aqueous outflow through an immature trabecular meshwork.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Trabeculodysgenesis — failure of the iridocorneal angle to mature properly during embryogenesis — is the primary mechanism. It is NOT pupil block (that is PACG), and NOT trabecular dysfunction from ageing (that is POAG).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Trabeculodysgenesis is the defining pathology. The arrested angle development leaves a thick, imperforate membrane over the trabecular meshwork, impeding aqueous drainage and raising IOP.
